question.text: An NRI has sale and investment proceeds from investments funded out of his NRO account that he now wishes to repatriate abroad. What is the maximum amount he can repatriate per financial year from such NRO-funded investment proceeds?

answer.text: USD 500,000 per financial year after applicable taxes
There is no limit on repatriation from NRO account as it is freely repatriable
USD 1 million per financial year, subject to applicable taxes
Funds in an NRO account are completely non-repatriable under any circumstances

explanation.text: The Logic: Investment or sale proceeds attributable to NRO-funded investments are repatriable only up to USD 1 million per financial year, subject to applicable taxes. This USD 1 million ceiling is the workbook-stated limit for repatriation from such NRO-sourced amounts. The Trap: Income earned in India such as rent, dividends, or pension is treated differently — it is freely repatriable after applicable Indian taxes are paid. The USD 1 million ceiling applies to investment or sale proceeds funded out of the NRO account, not to current-income items like rent. Note: Source basis is p.309 of the NISM-Series-X-A Investment Adviser (Level 1) workbook (June 2025), which separates NRO investment proceeds (capped at USD 1 million per financial year) from current income such as rent (freely repatriable after taxes).
